name: Ravbarkomanda Viaduct
place: A1 between Planina and Postojna, Postojna
zag_role: Long-term structural health monitoring and bridge weigh-in-motion
description: Two parallel structures carrying one direction each, built in 1972 on what is now the Venice to Lviv corridor. ZAG instrumented span P14D of the right-hand viaduct with strain gauges on the bottom flange of four main girders at mid-span, and triaxial accelerometers across several spans for ambient and traffic-induced modal testing. A bridge weigh-in-motion system supplies the traffic loading, and the measured response is used to update a finite element model of the structure. Both viaducts were fully rehabilitated between May 2017 and June 2019, including carbon fibre strengthening of the cantilevers, bearing replacement and a one metre deck widening.
history: Ravbarkomanda is a twin multi span precast I girder viaduct on the fifth Trans European corridor, which runs from Venice to Lviv. The right viaduct is about 595 m long with seventeen spans and the left viaduct about 556 m long with fifteen spans, and each carries two lanes and a hard shoulder. The monitoring system installed during the rehabilitation comprises 216 sensors measuring longitudinal strain on main girders, pier caps and deck extensions, temperature sensors across several spans, accelerometers on external prestressing tendons at 24 locations across both viaducts, 40 fibre Bragg grating sensors on carbon fibre rods, and long gauge deformation sensors at six pier cap locations per viaduct. Strain gauges record at 500 samples per second with a 35 Hz low pass filter. The structure crosses a double track railway line and a state road twice.

source_differences: length and spans: 588 m and 544 m, 15 spans left and 17 right (mdpi.com) against '560 m long', '16-span' (Sensors 2024) (mdpi.com)
length: 'dolg nekaj manj kot 600 metrov' (rtvslo.si) against 'both viaducts in the length of 600 m' (kolektor.cr74.creatim.serv.si)
end of rehabilitation: 'May 2017-July 2019' (kolektor.cr74.creatim.serv.si) against 'lasted from May 2017 to June 2019' (kolektor.com)

Deck lengths: the rehabilitation designer gives 595 m right and 556 m left, DARS gives 591.4 m right and 545.6 m left, and the Sensors 2023 paper gives 588 m and 544 m without naming the side. In all sources that name the side the longer deck is the right one, so the record text that puts 588 m on the left viaduct is not supported.
